text: MySuper Balanced Option is the default accumulation product for members who have not made an active investment choice. Target allocation is approximately 70 percent growth assets and 30 percent defensive assets. Indicative management fee 0.65 percent, plus an administration fee of 0.10 percent per annum.

Superannuation Growth Option targets long-term capital growth through a higher allocation to Australian and international shares and property. Suited to members with a long time horizon to retirement who can tolerate higher short-term volatility. Indicative management fee 0.75 percent.

Superannuation Conservative Option targets capital stability with a higher allocation to cash and fixed interest and a lower allocation to growth assets. May suit members close to or in retirement who want to limit exposure to market volatility. Indicative management fee 0.45 percent.

Account-Based Pension converts a member's accumulated superannuation balance into a regular income stream in retirement. Minimum annual payment amounts are set as a percentage of the account balance and increase with the member's age. Indicative management fee 0.55 percent.

Transition to Retirement Income Stream allows members who have reached preservation age but not retired to draw a limited income from superannuation while continuing to work. Annual payments are capped at 10 percent of the account balance. Indicative management fee 0.55 percent.

Ethical or Socially Responsible super option excludes companies involved in fossil fuels, tobacco, gambling and weapons manufacturing, and applies positive screening for environmental and governance factors. Indicative management fee 0.70 percent.

Employers must make Superannuation Guarantee contributions on behalf of eligible employees at the legislated minimum percentage of ordinary time earnings, paid at least quarterly into the employee's chosen complying fund.

Concessional and non-concessional contribution caps limit the amount that can be added to superannuation each financial year at concessional tax treatment or after-tax, and advice recommending contributions must flag any risk of exceeding the applicable cap.

Superannuation benefits are generally preserved until a member reaches preservation age and satisfies a condition of release such as retirement, reaching age 65, permanent incapacity, or a recognised compassionate or financial hardship ground.

metadata.title: Sample Preservation and Condition of Release Rule

text: Trustees and advisers must apply the sole purpose test, ensuring superannuation funds are maintained solely to provide retirement, death or disability benefits to members and not for any collateral purpose.

Under the Retirement Income Covenant, trustees must formulate, review and give effect to a retirement income strategy that assists members to maximise retirement income, manage risks to the sustainability and stability of that income, and have flexible access to savings.

MySuper products must meet authorisation requirements including a single diversified investment strategy or lifecycle option, standard fee structure, and are the default destination for employer contributions where a member has not made an active choice.

Advice recommending a member switch, consolidate or roll over superannuation must be in the member's best interests, weighing exit fees, insurance cover lost on exit, differences in investment options and total fees between the existing and recommended funds.

metadata.title: Sample Superannuation Switching Best Interests Rule

text: Advice affecting a member's default insurance held inside superannuation, including life, total and permanent disability and income protection cover, must disclose any change in premiums, cover level or underwriting terms resulting from the recommendation.

Account-based pension accounts are subject to legislated minimum annual drawdown percentages that increase with the member's age, and advice must confirm projected drawdowns satisfy the applicable minimum for the relevant financial year.
